{{nihongo|'''Ikota Shrine'''|伊居太神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Shimosakabe, {{ill|Amagasaki|Q213318|qid=Q213318}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. {{nihongo|'''Ikota Shrine'''|伊居太神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

It is one of the {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} identified as the {{ill|Ikota Shrine|ja|伊居太神社|qid=Q11379328}} listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} in {{ill|Kawabe District, Hyōgo|ceb|Kawanabe-gun|es|Distrito de Kawabe|fr|District de Kawabe|id|Distrik Kawabe, Hyōgo|it|Distretto di Kawabe|ja|川辺郡|ko|가와베군|pl|Powiat Kawabe|ru|Кавабе (уезд, Хёго)|zh|川邊郡|qid=Q1042053|lt=Kawabe District}}, {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}} (the other being {{ill|Ikeda, Osaka|ar|إكيدا (أوساكا)|arz|ايكيدا, اوساكا|ca|Ikeda (Osaka)|ce|Икеда (Осака)|ceb|Ikeda Shi|cy|Ikeda, Osaka|de|Ikeda (Osaka)|eo|Ikeda (Osaka)|es|Ikeda (Osaka)|et|Ikeda|fa|ایکه‌دا، اوساکا|fi|Ikeda (Osaka)|fr|Ikeda|gl|Ikeda, Ōsaka|it|Ikeda (Osaka)|ja|池田市|ko|이케다시|ms|Ikeda|mzn|ایکه‌دا، اوساکا|nl|Ikeda|no|Ikeda|pl|Ikeda (Osaka)|pt|Ikeda|ro|Ikeda, Osaka|ru|Икеда (Осака)|sh|Ikeda|sr|Икеда|sv|Ikeda, Ōsaka|szl|Ikeda|tg|Икеда|th|อิเกดะ (จังหวัดโอซากะ)|tl|Ikeda, Osaka|tr|Ikeda, Osaka|tt|Икеда (Осака)|uk|Ікеда (Осака)|ur|اکیڈا، اوساکا|vi|Ikeda, Ōsaka|war|Ikeda, Osaka|zh|池田市|zh_classical|池田市|zh_min_nan|Ikeda-chhī|zh_yue|池田|qid=Q817965}}’s {{ill|Ikeda Shrine|ja|伊居太神社 (池田市)|qid=Q11379329|lt=Ikota Shrine}} (Ikeda Shrine)).

== History ==
The area was the residence of the {{ill|Sakaibe Clan|ja|坂合部氏|qid=Q85878332}}, and the shrine originally enshrined the clan’s {{ill|Lord mayor|ar|اللورد العمدة|be|Обер-бургамістр|da|Overborgmester|et|Ülemlinnapea|fi|Ylipormestari|fr|Lord-maire|frr|Boowerbürgermääster|he|הלורד ראש העיר|id|Lord Mayor|it|Lord Mayor|ja|首長|nds|Böverbörgermeester|no|Overborgermester|pnb|لارڈ میئر|ru|Обер-бургомистр|sco|Laird Mayor|simple|Lord Mayor|sv|Överborgmästare|uk|Обер-бургомістр|ur|لارڈ میئر|zh|首長|qid=Q11902879}}, {{ill|Ōhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|大彦命|zh|大彦命|qid=Q11435420}}, and his descendants. It is believed that when the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ar|فوجيوارا (عشيرة)|be|Фудзівара (род)|br|Klann Fujiwara|ca|Clan Fujiwara|cs|Fudžiwara|de|Fujiwara (Familie)|el|Αδελφότητα Φούτζιγουαρα|es|Clan Fujiwara|eu|Fujiwara klana|fa|خاندان فوجیوارا|fi|Fujiwara-klaani|fr|Clan Fujiwara|he|בית פוג'יווארה|hr|Fujiwara (klan)|hu|Fudzsivara család|id|Klan Fujiwara|it|Clan Fujiwara|ja|藤原氏|ko|후지와라씨|la|Domus Fujiwara|ms|Suku Fujiwara|nl|Fujiwara (familie)|pl|Fujiwara (ród)|pt|Clã Fujiwara|ru|Фудзивара (род)|sh|Fujiwara (klan)|sk|Fudžiwara|sr|Фуџивара клан|sv|Fujiwara|ta|புஜிவாரா குலம்|th|ตระกูลฟูจิวาระ|tr|Fujiwara boyu|uk|Рід Фудзівара|vi|Gia tộc Fujiwara|zh|藤原氏|zh_classical|藤原氏|zh_min_nan|Fujiwara--sī|qid=Q641628}} came to control the area, they invited ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kanjō}}) the deities of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ca|Gran santuari de Kasuga|co|Grandi Santuariu Kasuga|cs|Svatyně Kasuga|de|Kasuga-Taisha|es|Kasuga-taisha|eu|Kasuga-taisha|fa|کاسوگا-تایشا|fi|Kasuga-taisha|fr|Kasuga-taisha|he|מקדש קאסוגה|id|Kuil Agung Kasuga|it|Santuario Kasuga|ja|春日大社|ka|კასუგა-ტაისია|ko|가스가타이샤|la|Kasuga-taisha|pl|Kasuga Taisha|pt|Kasuga-taisha|ru|Касуга тайся|sh|Kasuga-taisha|simple|Kasuga Taisha|sl|Svetišče Kasuga|th|ศาลเจ้าคาซูงะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Kasuka|tr|Kasuga-taisha|uk|Касуга тайся|zh|春日大社|qid=Q714559}} here.<ref>Ikota Shrine, “Coastline and Origins” (1999).</ref>

“Osaka-fu Zenshi” identifies the {{ill|Ikeda Shrine|ja|伊居太神社 (池田市)|qid=Q11379329|lt=Ikota Shrine}} in Ikeda City as the Shikinaisha, stating that it was relocated ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=senzā}}) from Kosakata Village in {{ill|Kawabe District, Hyōgo|ceb|Kawanabe-gun|es|Distrito de Kawabe|fr|District de Kawabe|id|Distrik Kawabe, Hyōgo|it|Distretto di Kawabe|ja|川辺郡|ko|가와베군|pl|Powiat Kawabe|ru|Кавабе (уезд, Хёго)|zh|川邊郡|qid=Q1042053}} (present-day {{ill|Itami|ar|إتامي (هيوغو)|az|İtami|azb|ایتامی، هیوقو|ca|Itami|ce|Итами|cs|Itami|de|Itami|eo|Itami|es|Itami (Hyōgo)|et|Itami|fa|ایتامی، هیوگو|fi|Itami|fr|Itami|gl|Itami|hy|Իտամի|it|Itami|ja|伊丹市|ko|이타미시|lt|Itamis|mg|Itami|mzn|ایتامی، هیوگو|nl|Itami|no|Itami|pl|Itami|pt|Itami|ro|Itami|ru|Итами|sh|Itami|simple|Itami|sr|Итами|sv|Itami|tg|Итами|th|อิตามิ|tl|Itami|tr|Itami|tt|Итами|uk|Ітамі|ur|اتامی|uz|Itami|vi|Itami, Hyōgo|war|Itami, Hyōgo|zh|伊丹市|zh_classical|伊丹市|zh_min_nan|Itami-chhī|zh_yue|伊丹|qid=Q335444}}) to {{ill|Toyono District, Osaka|Q1205516|qid=Q1205516}}.
This view follows the theory of “Settsushi,” but there is also the argument that “judging from the {{ill|jōri system|Q11523645|qid=Q11523645}}, it should be Toyoshima District rather than Kawabe District, meaning the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}} made an error regarding the district.”<ref>Shiga Tsuyoshi, “Study of Shikinaisha, Vol. 3” (1977), {{National Bibliography Number|77010794}}.</ref>

The “Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer” states: “The Ikota Shrine in Ikeda Town, Toyono District, Osaka Prefecture, stands at the site of the Kureori Shrine of Kureori Village. With the prosperity of the region in the medieval period, this shrine, which enshrined Anaori Ōkami, was relocated to the entrance of the town and revered as the {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}}. The Kureori Shrine was designated as its {{ill|Otabisho|Q11489117|qid=Q11489117}}, and eventually the Kureori Shrine came to be called Ikota Shrine as well.”<ref>Yoshii Sadatoshi, “Shikinaisha Survey Report, Vol. 5” (1977), {{National Bibliography Number|78005760}}.</ref>
In terms of old place names, the Ikota Shrine enshrined at this location is considered to correspond to the original.

In January {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 7 (1995), the shrine buildings collapsed due to the {{ill|Damage by Great Hanshin earthquake|Q11392882|qid=Q11392882}}, and new buildings were reconstructed in April Heisei 11 (1999).

'''Ikota Kofun''' (いこたこふん) was a {{ill|Kofun|Q1141225|qid=Q1141225}} that once stood within the precincts of Ikota Shrine. Its shape was a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|ko|전방후원분|simple|Zenpō-kōen-fun|zh|前方後圓墳|qid=Q11268718}}. Today, the burial mound has been lost.

The tomb was keyhole-shaped, with the front portion facing south. The mound dimensions are as follows (based on a survey conducted in {{ill|1963|Q2755|qid=Q2755}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 38)){{Sfn|Ikota Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}:
* Total length: approx. 92 meters
* Rear circular portion diameter: approx. 46 meters
* Front portion width: approx. 53 meters
This makes it the largest kofun in Amagasaki City.<ref name="尼崎市"/> A surrounding moat encircled the mound, measuring approximately 20 meters in width{{Sfn|Ikota Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. No excavated artifacts are known.<ref name="尼崎市">[http://www2.city.amagasaki.hyogo.jp/bunkazai/siseki/ikota_kofun/ikota_kofun.html Ikota Kofun] (Amagasaki City website).</ref>

This Ikota Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|5th century|Q8095|qid=Q8095}}, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}}{{Sfn|Ikota Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. The interred individual is unknown, but Ikota Shrine maintains that it is the tomb of the ancestral deity of the Sakaibe no Muraji (Sakaibe clan), and that the shrine was built atop this tomb.<ref name="由緒書">Shrine origin document.</ref> On the south side of the front portion, there were once two mounds known as Samurai-zuka and Hakuba-zuka, which are said to have been {{ill|Baizuka|Q11658220|qid=Q11658220}} of Ikota Kofun.<ref name="由緒書"/>

However, to date, archaeological excavations have not produced definitive evidence proving that Ikota Kofun was indeed a kofun.<ref>“The Inagawa River Basin in the Kofun Period – Movements of the Kinai Polity Projected onto the Inagawa Basin – (Ikeda City Museum of History and Folklore, Heisei 22 Special Exhibition),” Ikeda City Museum of History and Folklore, 2010.</ref>

== Excavation history ==
* {{ill|1950|Q18597|qid=Q18597}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 25): Test excavation at the center of the rear circular portion. No clear structures or artifacts confirmed{{Sfn|Ikota Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}.
* {{ill|1963|Q2755|qid=Q2755}} (Shōwa 38): Survey measurement{{Sfn|Ikota Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}.
* From {{ill|1965|Q2650|qid=Q2650}} (Shōwa 40) onward: Land readjustment projects significantly altered the moat area{{Sfn|Ikota Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}.
* Recent years: Excavations in the presumed moat area. No structures or artifacts confirmed{{Sfn|Ikota Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}.

== Access ==
* 15-minute walk east from {{ill|Tsukaguchi Station (JR West)|Q847972|qid=Q847972|lt=Tsukaguchi Station}} on the {{ill|Fukuchiyama Line|Q1154538|qid=Q1154538|lt=JR Takarazuka Line}}.
* Immediately after getting off at Chikamatsu Park on the city bus.
